Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (Redwood Product), Evan Chen (CTO, Cedar Data), Lina Ortiz (ML Eng), Marcus Lee (Head of Security), Jada Park (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick demo of JSON-mode structured output and guarded tool calling. Customer emphasizes auditability and deterministic fallbacks. Agreed to benchmark and share security docs.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for taking the time, good to see you all. we'll do a 45 minute walkthrough and then leave ~10 minutes for q and a. is that still okay on your side?
[00:10] Evan (CTO): yeah that's perfect, we got time. thanks Alex.
[00:14] Priya (SE): cool, i'll share my screen in a sec. quick agenda: show JSON mode + schema enforcement, tool calls with guardrails, runtime fallbacks, and then pilot ideas.
[00:25] Jada (PM): can you start with a quick reminder of how JSON mode differs from just parsing text please?
[00:30] Priya (SE): sure, so JSON mode forces the model to emit a strict schema. think of it like contract first - we validate at runtime and can automatically route to tools based on typed fields. it reduces flakiness, especially when you're chaining calls.
[00:45] Lina (ML Eng): and does that work with function calling - like we want to call an internal enrichment API but only if confidence > 0.8?
[00:52] Priya (SE): yep, you can annotate the field with a confidence score and express a guard: call enrich_api only if confidence >= 0.8. Runtime enforces that and we never fire side-effects outside the sandbox unless guard passes.
[01:05] Marcus (Security): quick security question - how do you prove what the model did? we need audit logs and tamper evidence for compliance.
[01:12] Sam (Product): good point. we surface token-level traces, the schema of the output, and every tool invocation in the audit log. logs are signed and can be routed to your SIEM; we also integrate with KMS for key rotation.
[01:25] Evan (CTO): are the logs stored in Redwood or forwarded to our S3? we prefer not to persist any customer PII in a third party.
[01:33] Alex (AE): you can choose. hosted keeps logs but you can configure retention and redaction. for private or dedicated we can forward logs to your bucket and apply HSM-backed signing via your KMS.
[01:45] [screenshare begins - demo]
[02:05] Priya (SE): ok here's a sample prompt set from Cedar — a ticket enrichment flow. we show the schema first: {"ticket_id": "string", "priority": "enum(low,med,high)", "enqueue_api_call": "boolean", "confidence": "number"} - model must return valid JSON.
[02:25] Lina (ML Eng): i can see that reducing downstream parsing errors. what about partial outputs when a model times out?
[02:32] Priya (SE): good question. we support partial outputs with a validation stage. if partial output doesn't match schema, runtime can either reject and fallback to a simpler model or call a deterministic fallback path. you configure policy per route.
[02:48] Evan (CTO): give us an example of a fallback policy please.
[02:52] Priya (SE): sure — first try: high-quality open model with quantization off for best accuracy; if latency or token budget breached, fallback to a distilled variant that supports same schema; if that fails, return a canonical safe-output (a neutral JSON object) and log the event.
[03:10] Marcus (Security): how do you guarantee the fallback doesn't call our side-effect API if it's not allowed?
[03:15] Priya (SE): we have enforced tool gating. tool call permissions live in RBAC and route policies. only routes with explicit permission can invoke external APIs; fallbacks inherit the same gating and cannot escalate.
[03:28] [demo: function call wiring]
[03:40] Priya (SE): here's the function binding. note the typed signature: enrich_api(user_id: string, fields: list[string]) -> {status: string, changes: list[string], confidence: number}. Redwood validates the arguments before invocation and logs the call.
[03:55] Lina (ML Eng): does Redwood serialize the exact model tokens used for the decision? we need that for reproducibility.
[04:02] Priya (SE): we capture prompts, responses, token-level deltas when requested. that's optional for cost reasons but doable for audit runs.
[04:15] Evan (CTO): can you show the runtime routing UI in the console?
[04:20] Sam (Product): sure. switching to console - this is a per-route policy page. you can set latency SLOs, cost targets, and map model variants. here's an example: default route uses rdm-large, fallback rdm-small, emergency region fallback to Dedicated-EU.
[05:00] Alex (AE): we often see customers trade a bit of latency for cost; the console shows estimated per-1000 token unit economics for each model variant.
[05:12] Jada (PM): who owns model catalog updates? we have internal fine-tuned models too.
[05:18] Priya (SE): you can onboard your model artifacts to Private mode, or we can host a pinned model variant in Dedicated. the catalog records versioning and you can lock a route to a specific version for rollouts.
[05:34] [demo: error handling and typed fallbacks]
[06:05] Priya (SE): here we force an invalid schema response to trigger the fallback. note the trace — we show the schema mismatch, the policy evaluation, and the final safe-output. everything is recorded.
[06:25] Marcus (Security): how do we control who in our org can change policies?
[06:30] Sam (Product): RBAC in the console ties to SSO groups. we also surface an approval workflow for policy changes so a change requires two approvers if you choose.
[06:45] Evan (CTO): what about data residency? our EU customers mandate EU-only processing.
[06:50] Alex (AE): we have region-aware routing and Private deployments in customer VPCs. you can pin a route to EU-only inference and logs forwarding.
[06:58] Lina (ML Eng): let's talk about developer ergonomics - do you have SDKs for typed outputs and local contract checking?
[07:05] Priya (SE): yes - SDKs in python and node. we provide client-side schema validators and a local contract-checker that runs in your CI to catch regressions before rollout.
[07:20] Evan (CTO): demo the dev flow - schema -> tests -> deploy, please.
[07:25] Priya (SE): quick sequence: author schema in console or repo, run local checker, push prompts + tests to Redwood evals; Redwood will run regression tests against golden prompt sets and block rollout if metrics dip.
[07:45] Jada (PM): how do you measure quality drift for these structured outputs?
[07:50] Priya (SE): we compute schema conformance, semantic score on key fields, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. you can set thresholds to trigger canary rollback.
[08:05] Evan (CTO): i saw in your docs mention of KV cache and prefix caching - does that affect typed outputs?
[08:12] Priya (SE): caching only affects hot-prefixes. typed outputs are deterministic per model+prompt but cache can speed up repeated prompts. the runtime ensures cache hits still validate schema before returning.
[08:25] [screen transitions: sandbox tool invocation]
[09:00] Priya (SE): here we have a sandboxed enrich_api. note we simulate latency and show the pre-check: input validated, guard passed, then call executed. the console shows request, payload, and response.
[09:30] Lina (ML Eng): sometimes our enrichment can drop fields; does Redwood allow partial rollbacks on fields?
[09:36] Priya (SE): we support transactional semantics for tool chains in Private mode. you can either commit the whole output or abort and return safe-output depending on policy.
[09:50] Marcus (Security): how do you prevent data exfiltration via tools? e.g., model asks tool for dataset dump.
[09:58] Priya (SE): tools are whitelisted and argument-validated. we also do pattern-based argument scanning and block suspicious calls; plus RBAC limits which routes can call which tools.
[10:15] Evan (CTO): operationally, if we see more failures in canary, can we auto-fallback to a simpler rule-based enrich?
[10:22] Priya (SE): yes - you can configure automatic fallback to a deterministic rule engine or a cached response. the routing layer supports multi-step fallbacks.
[10:35] [Q&A - deeper technical digging]
[11:05] Evan (CTO): Priya, for the benchmark you mentioned, what metrics will you run?
[11:10] Priya (SE): latency P50/P95/P99, schema-conformance rate, tool-invocation accuracy, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also run failure-mode scenarios to exercise fallbacks.
[11:20] Lina (ML Eng): for the schema conformance, is that strict equality or fuzzy matching on field semantics?
[11:27] Priya (SE): schema conformance is structural (types, required fields). semantic checks are separate evals where we score field values against golden labels.
[11:40] Marcus (Security): what's the data retention for audit logs in Hosted?
[11:45] Alex (AE): default 90 days; customizable for enterprise contracts. for Private you control retention.
[11:55] Jada (PM): timeline question - we aim to pilot before year-end. is that realistic?
[12:00] Alex (AE): yes, with a 2-4 week pilot. depends on dataset readiness and security review.
[12:10] Evan (CTO): ok we can try to get redacted dataset by Friday.
[12:15] [demo wrap-up]
[12:30] Priya (SE): demo notes — guard expressions, typed signatures, RBAC for tools, signed audit logs, and fallback primitives.
[12:40] Evan (CTO): this looks promising. two quick asks: show us the SOC2 artifacts and an SSO setup doc.
[12:48] Alex (AE): will do. Sam, you take SOW?
[12:52] Sam (Product): yep, i'll draft SOW and pricing options.
[12:55] Alex (AE): thanks everyone, we will follow up with the recording and action items.
[13:00] [meeting ends]
